fields.name: post_button_target
fields.description: During the video cycle, locate the hand's downward press on the gray button on its white base. Follow the instructed-color cube after that press to its next target placement. Save the earliest shown frame where it has been released there and the hand has lifted enough to distinguish release from continued holding. Do not select its pre-press target or its subsequent off-target reset position. At every act cycle copy the incoming label unchanged. e.g. "V448"
fields.annotation: At the video cycle, record the earliest shown frame in which the instructed cube has been released onto the first target it is placed on after the button press, with the hand lifted enough to distinguish the released cube from a held cube. Ignore the target occupied before the press and the later off-target reset placement. Carry this frame label unchanged through all act cycles. For the supplied episodes the labels are respectively V448, V480, V448, V512, and V432. e.g. "V448"

action:
At the video cycle output memory only. Execution begins with an open hand above the table and the instructed-color cube at its reset position. The instruction refers to a temporal relationship in the demonstration: place the cube on the target used immediately after the demonstrated button press. Do not press the button in execution, replay the earlier placement, or wait for a new button event.

Use post_button_target to identify the purple ring underneath the released instructed-color cube in the saved demonstration frame. Match that ring to the current scene using the stationary ring layout and button. This is the destination, even if another ring is closer to the cube. Ignore cubes of other colors.

Estimate world positions using calibrated camera rays. Intersect ring-center rays with the tabletop plane z=0. Estimate cube horizontal center using its top face at approximately z=0.04 rather than projecting its image center onto the table. Use the current wrist view to refine alignment. Orient the hand straight down, roll approximately pi and pitch zero, with yaw aligned to the cube's horizontal edges; maintain that orientation while carrying and releasing it.

Apply these observable-state rules: If the hand is open, the cube is not already on the remembered destination, and the hand is not at its pickup approach, move above the cube center to z=0.15 with gripper open. If the open hand is at this approach (allowing normal endpoint error), descend to the cube center at z=0.02 and close. If the cube is grasped and the hand is low at pickup, lift vertically to z=0.15 with gripper closed. If holding the cube at clearance height but not above the destination, move horizontally to the destination center at z=0.15 with gripper closed. If holding the cube above the destination at clearance height, descend at that destination center to commanded z=0.005 and open. If the hand is open and low over the cube released onto the destination, retract vertically to z=0.15 with gripper open. Do not mistake a recently released cube for a fresh pickup; its position on the remembered destination and the open fingers establish the retreat condition. Do not insist that the measured release height equal 0.005: contact can leave the TCP around 0.01–0.02.

Use approximate arrival tolerances of 0.02 m at approach height and 0.01 m horizontally above the destination, refining the actual destination from the visible ring rather than substituting the imperfect reached TCP position. Preserve closed fingers throughout lift and transport. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint merely to change the gripper; include at least 0.002 m of movement.

For an unrecognized or ambiguous state, use the visible grasp and geometry to recover: lift a securely held cube to clearance before lateral movement; with an empty hand, move open to a clear elevated observation pose and relocalize the instructed cube and remembered ring. Do not choose a different target because the intended one is occluded. If the cube is already correctly placed, withdraw without disturbing it.
